title: Unify credential telemetry and declarative stream guardrails across Py/TS/Go
author: Ava Morales
release_notes: Adds CredentialSnapshotter telemetry and a lightweight declarative StreamGuard across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Minor ergonomic facades for async streams. Bumps SDK versions: py 1.12.0, ts 2.7.0, go 1.5.2.
description: Motivation: Different SDKs implemented ad-hoc credential prefetch and streaming guard code over time which made telemetry sparse and client ergonomics inconsistent. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialSnapshotter with observable lifecycle events and a declarative StreamGuard primitive that standardizes precondition checks, early cancellation hooks, and common retry/backoff presets across Python, TypeScript, and Go. The goal is improved operational visibility (why a request reauth'd / was prefetched) and a single ergonomic story for streaming consumers without changing runtime behavior for most callers. Changes are additive and guarded by opt-in configuration.

feat(stream): add StreamGuard spec and lightweight implementations for py/ts/go
refactor(sdk): unify telemetry event names and wire up to existing auth-layer
test: integration tests for prefetch timing and stream cancellation semantics
docs: migration guide and examples (py/ts/go) and changelogs
chore: bump versions (py 1.12.0, ts 2.7.0, go 1.5.2) and update changelogs

review_comments: Rohit: Nice consolidation. Can we keep the default snapshot TTL unchanged for hosted customers? Also add a metric for dropped prefetches (when snapshot is stale on apply).
Author (Ava): Kept hosted default identical; added metric 'cred.prefetch.dropped' and unit tests covering the stale path.
Lina: The StreamGuard API looks good for TS/py; in Go the channel-based cancel semantics feel a little clunky. Consider adding a small helper ChannelGuard that yields a cancel func.
Author: Added ChannelGuard helper and an example in examples/go demonstrating graceful drain.
Marek: CI flaky e2e observed; one run failed on a timing sensitive test. Can we make test less timing dependent?
Author: Relaxed timing assertion and replaced a hard sleep with a time-check loop; CI reran and passed.
Rohit: Please add an entry in each SDK changelog and the top-level migration doc with clear opt-in instructions.
Author: Done — changelogs and docs/sdk/migration/credential-snapshotter.md added with code snippets.
ci_summary: All unit suites passed (py/ts/go). One e2e run failed on the first attempt for a timing-sensitive stream cancellation test; test adjusted and rerun succeeded. Lint and typechecks (mypy/tsc/golangci) passed. Integration matrix: linux, macos, node16, go1.20 all green.
notes_for_backport: Backport to v1.11.x only if customers require explicit prefetch metrics (add changelog note)
Do not backport the StreamGuard ergonomics to legacy TS <2.0 — new async iterator helpers rely on async generator support
